messages:
maria: Quick question — I'm updating the payments Helm chart to support optional ExternalSecret wiring. Goal: render envFrom when a secret exists (either created by ExternalSecret or provided manually), but avoid rendering an empty secretRef when there's no name. Current snippet in chart is `envFrom:\n  - secretRef:\n      name: {{ .Values.service.secretName }}` which renders an empty name sometimes. Anyone got a clean templating pattern for this? Also, this change will be paired with a Terraform change to create the ExternalSecret CR — any deployment ordering concerns? pinging @raj for chart review :wave:

raj: You can guard the block with a simple `if` check. Helm treats missing/null values as falsy, so prefer null over empty string in values.yaml. Example pattern that I use: 

```
{{- if .Values.service.secretName }}
envFrom:
  - secretRef:
      name: {{ .Values.service.secretName | quote }}
{{- end }}
```

raj: If you need to prefer an ExternalSecret name when present but fallback to a static secret, expose two values and compute in templates. e.g.:

```
{{- $name := default .Values.service.fallbackSecret .Values.service.externalSecretName }}
{{- if $name }}
envFrom:
  - secretRef:
      name: {{ $name | quote }}
{{- end }}
```

hugo: small nit — make sure your values file sets `service.secretName: null` when not provided. Empty string will still render if you check `ne` vs `if`. Also `| quote` avoids weird YAML when name includes special chars.

emma: Terraform/CI note: our pipeline currently applies k8s resources (ExternalSecret via terraform-provider-kubernetes) and then runs Helm. In practice the ExternalSecret controller reconciles async and may not create the actual Secret instantly. So even if TF creates the ExternalSecret CR before Helm, the Secret might appear later. Options: (1) add a post-helm `kubectl wait` step that checks for the Secret, (2) run helm with `--wait` which may block too long on GH runners, or (3) sequence workloads so the app deployment is rolled after secret is present. I'll open a small change to our release job to add an optional wait.

infra-bot: Current pipeline status: helm upgrade --install used without --wait. Suggestion: add a lightweight post-deploy check in the release job that does `kubectl get secret <name> -n <ns> || (sleep 2; retry...)` up to e.g. 60s. Pseudocode in CI job: 

```
# after helm upgrade
for i in {1..30}; do
  if kubectl -n $NS get secret $SECRET_NAME >/dev/null 2>&1; then
    echo "secret present"; break
  fi
  sleep 2
done
```

infra-bot: Alternatively we can add an annotation to the Helm release job to skip starting the deployment until secret is present, but the above loop is simplest.

maria: :thumbsup: thanks! I'll: 1) switch values.yaml to use null defaults, 2) add the `if` guard in templates, 3) add the small post-release secret-check to CI, and 4) open the Terraform PR to create ExternalSecret earlier. I'll ping for chart + pipeline review when PRs are up.
